purpose: Operate Swell as one evidence-backed system from market signal through acquisition, onboarding, delivery, retention, feedback, and advocacy.
operatingPrinciples: One account identity and append-only activity history across the entire client lifecycle.
A stage represents verified state, never agent activity or intent.
Every open commercial, onboarding, delivery, and client-success record has one owner, one next action, and one due date.
Agents may prepare and execute reversible work inside approved scope; material commitments and irreversible external actions require the authority defined here.
No campaign is launched without an approved brief, validated tracking, a rollback path, and an accountable owner.
No result, testimonial, review, or case study is fabricated, selectively misrepresented, or published without client permission.
Automation failures are visible, replayable, and owned. Silent failure is a launch blocker.

systemsOfRecord.rule: Identifiers are linked across systems; confidential artifacts are not copied into general CRM notes.

clientLifecycle.definition: Agreement and required initial payment are verified; delivery has not accepted the commercial record.
Stakeholders, communication rules, access, evidence, measurement, and kickoff outcomes are being verified.
The baseline and strategy are approved, capacity is assigned, and the first campaign or delivery cycle is ready for launch review.
Approved work is being executed and measured within scope.
The engagement is inside its renewal decision window and has a documented outcome and next-term recommendation.
Scoped work and acceptance are complete; final reporting, access disposition, and follow-up are in progress.
Work is intentionally paused with a reason, impact, owner, and review date.
Work is closed, access is removed or transferred, artifacts are delivered, and permitted follow-up is scheduled.

workItemDefinition.completionRule: A work item is accepted only when its acceptance evidence is recorded.

autonomous: Research public sources and approved client repositories
Normalize, deduplicate, classify, summarize, and score records
Draft briefs, plans, copy, reports, tasks, and internal recommendations
Create internal tasks and route work using approved rules
Monitor approved campaigns, budgets, deadlines, delivery quality, and client health
Pause an automation or campaign when a documented safety or spend stop condition fires
Send approved transactional confirmations after destination success
policyBound: Send follow-up using an approved template, consent scope, audience, channel, and frequency policy
Schedule approved assets and campaigns without changing claims, audience, channel, or budget
Apply optimizations inside the approved brief's spend, claim, channel, and experiment bounds
Request missing onboarding inputs and send factual status reports using approved communication rules
humanApprovalRequired: Change pricing, discounting, payment terms, scope, or contractual commitments
Mark an opportunity closed won without verified agreement and required payment
Accept credentials, change account permissions, or grant third-party access
Approve strategy, a new public claim, creative direction, or a campaign's first launch
Increase budget or expand audience, geography, channel, or data use beyond the approved brief
Issue refunds, credits, legal responses, or regulated claims
Publish a testimonial, review, case study, client name, logo, or confidential result
Override consent, suppression, safety, quality, or acceptance gates
forbidden: Fabricate evidence, authority, performance, reviews, testimonials, identities, or consent
Purchase or use unlawfully obtained contact data
Send after opt-out or outside the recorded consent and outreach policy
Hide failures, spend, material negative results, or scope deviations
Store secrets in prompts, CRM notes, logs, or generated artifacts

sequence: Confirm delivery acceptance and resolve open issues.
Request private feedback without conditioning service or incentives on sentiment.
Route negative or unresolved feedback to service recovery.
Apply one neutral public-review outreach policy regardless of sentiment; delay only while a material service issue is unresolved or outreach is not permitted.
Request separate written permission for testimonial, logo, named results, or case-study use.
feedbackPolicy.reviewEligibilityRule: Eligible when delivery is accepted, the neutral private-feedback step is complete, no material service issue is open, and outreach is permitted; sentiment must not determine eligibility.

healthSignals.green: Milestones are on track, inputs and approvals arrive within SLA, outcomes are supported, and no material issue is open.
healthSignals.yellow: One material dependency, deadline, quality measure, usage signal, or stakeholder relationship is at risk.
healthSignals.red: A safety, consent, scope, payment, access, performance, or relationship issue threatens delivery or trust.

automationRequirements: Idempotency key and append-only source event
Destination confirmation before success is stated
Retry policy, dead-letter record, and failure owner
Success, duplicate, invalid, rejection, timeout, suppression, and recovery tests
